answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable, costly history, like a karst cave system where every passage is carved slowly by water over time. An agent earns trust only by accumulating a public record of useful work, layered like shale: each stratum of completed tasks is independently checkable. A newcomer with no strata carries no weight, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because forging a deep, ferrous-hard history for each one costs more than any sybil attack could extract.
